title: The infinitesimal induced Steinberg module is simple
statement:
Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], of prime characteristic $p>0$, and let $S$ be a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]. Semisimple means smooth, affine, connected and of finite type, with no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup, where solvable means that the successive commutator subgroup schemes eventually become trivial. Simply connected means that every surjective homomorphism $S'\to S$ from a semisimple group scheme with finite central kernel is an isomorphism; finite means finite-dimensional coordinate algebra and central means commuting with every element after every scalar extension. A split torus is a group scheme isomorphic to $\mathbf G_m^r$ for some $r\ge0$, where $\mathbf G_m(A)=A^\times$; a maximal torus is one not contained in a larger torus. A Borel subgroup is a maximal smooth connected solvable closed subgroup. Fix a split maximal torus $T\subseteq S$ and a Borel subgroup $B\supseteq T$. For this pair, let $\Phi^+$ be the positive roots given by the nonzero characters of the adjoint action of $T$ on $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$, where $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$ is the kernel of $B(F[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2))\to B(F)$, with its tangent-space structure. A character is a group-scheme homomorphism $T\to\mathbf G_m$; addition of characters means multiplication of their values. Let $\rho\in X^*(T)$ satisfy $2\rho=\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\alpha$, and let $\widetilde\rho:B\to\mathbf G_m$ extend it and be trivial on the unipotent radical of $B$; this radical is its largest smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup, with unipotent meaning that all geometric points are unipotent matrices in a faithful linear representation. Fix an integer $r\ge1$ and write $q=p^r$ and $\lambda=(q-1)\rho$. If $C=F[S]$, define $S^{(q)}=\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_{F,a\mapsto a^q}F)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]; its group operations are obtained by this base change. The relative Frobenius $F^r_{S/F}:S\to S^{(q)}$ has coordinate map $c\otimes a\mapsto ac^q$. Let $T^{(q)}\subseteq S^{(q)}$ be the base change of $T$, let $S_r=\ker F^r_{S/F}$, and define the closed subgroup schemes $L_r=(F^r_{S/F})^{-1}(T^{(q)})$ and $P_r=B\cap L_r$, with scheme-theoretic inverse image and intersection. Use the notation $S_rT=L_r$ and $B_rT=P_r$. On $P_r$ use the restriction of the given $B$-character $\widetilde\rho$. Define the actual infinitesimal induced module
$$Z_r=\{f\in F[L_r]:f(xb)=\widetilde\rho(b)^{q-1}f(x)\text{ for every commutative }F\text{-algebra }D,\ x\in L_r(D),\ b\in P_r(D)\}.$$
Use left translation $(h f)(x)=f(h^{-1}x)$. A rational module for an affine group scheme $K$ is an $F$-vector space with a coassociative counital coaction $M\to M\otimes_FF[K]$; a submodule is an $F$-linear subspace whose coaction lands in its tensor product with $F[K]$. Equivariance means equality of coactions, equivalently equality after every commutative $F$-algebra extension. Write $\widehat Z'_r(\lambda)=Z_r$ for this choice of positive roots in $\operatorname{Lie}(B)$. Left translation gives $Z_r$ a finite-dimensional simple rational $L_r$-module structure: $Z_r\ne0$, and the only $F$-linear subspaces stable under the $F[L_r]$-coaction are $0$ and $Z_r$. This includes the trivial group and all primes $p$, including $2$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-frobenius-kernel-induced-dual-pbw] with $\eta=(q-1)\rho$ and $\widetilde\eta=\widetilde\rho^{q-1}$. Its function space is exactly the stated $Z_r$. It gives a rational $L_r$-action, dimension $q^N$, an opposite Borel with radical $U^-$, and $M=A\otimes_{D_B}F_\lambda\simeq Z_r^\vee$ with $v=1\otimes1\ne0$ and $H=\operatorname{Dist}(U^-_r)\xrightarrow{\sim}M$, $h\mapsto hv$. The last assertion of [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure] makes $S$ reductive, so [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations] supplies root parametrizations for the positive and negative roots. Thus $Z_r\ne0$, and it remains to exclude proper nonzero submodules.

source.place: Q86 agent assembly of the infinitesimal route; finite-kernel evaluation duality (local book WANTED)

proof.text: Let $W\subseteq M$ be any nonzero $A$-submodule. Under $H\simeq M$, [lem-sfb-unipotent-frobenius-distribution-socle] gives a nilpotent augmentation ideal $J$ and $\operatorname{Ann}_M(J)=F f_{\rm top}v$. Choose the largest $n\ge0$ with $J^nW\ne0$, which exists since $J^m=0$ and $J^0W=W$. Then $0\ne J^nW\subseteq W\cap\operatorname{Ann}_M(J)$. A nonzero subspace of this one-dimensional line is the whole line, so $f_{\rm top}v\in W$.

source.place: Q86 agent assembly of the infinitesimal route; unipotent augmentation-socle argument (local book WANTED)

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-steinberg-top-distribution-recovery], $e_{\rm top}f_{\rm top}v=cv$ for some $c\in F^\times$. Since $e_{\rm top}\in A$ and $W$ is $A$-stable, $v\in W$. Every tensor $a\otimes t$ is $tav$, so $M=Av\subseteq W$. This proves that $M$ is simple as an $A$-module.

source.place: Q86 agent assembly of the infinitesimal route; top-root distribution calculation at Steinberg weight (local book WANTED)

proof.text: Let $V\subseteq Z_r$ be stable under the $L_r$-coaction. Restricting that coaction to $S_r$ shows $aV\subseteq V$ for every $a\in A$. Its annihilator $V^\perp\subseteq Z_r^\vee$ is $A$-stable: $(a\ell)(w)=\ell(\sigma(a)w)=0$ for $w\in V$, using the dual action in [lem-sfb-frobenius-kernel-induced-dual-pbw]. Identify it with a submodule of $M$. By the preceding steps it is $0$ or $M$. In a finite-dimensional vector space a proper subspace has a nonzero annihilating functional, by extending a basis; hence $V^\perp=0$ gives $V=Z_r$, whereas $V^\perp=Z_r^\vee$ gives $V=0$. Together with $\dim Z_r=q^N\ge1$, this is the required simplicity. For $S=1$ the products are empty and $Z_r=F$; none of the steps divides by a factorial or excludes $p=2$.
